title: SLO Cross-Team Mapping & Resource Runway
content:
Executive summary:

This document describes a focused campaign to operationalize SLOs across product and platform teams by creating a cross-team mapping, a 10-week resource runway, and clear handoff checkpoints. The intent is to reduce blind spots in ownership, prevent SLO drift, and ensure each service has a minimal, testable SLO + alerting + playbook within 10 weeks.

Goals (measurable):
- Inventory: catalog SLO candidates for 28 critical services within 3 weeks.
- Adoption: 75% of cataloged services have an initial SLO, alerting, and remediation playbook within 10 weeks.
- Observability: enable smoke dashboards for 100% of adopted SLOs and integrate with oncall routing.
- Stability improvement: reduce P95 latency regressions causing incidents by 30% over the first quarter post-adoption.

Scope and constraints:
- In-scope: customer-facing inference APIs, routing layer, KV cache infra, batching pipelines.
- Out-of-scope for this campaign: experimental model training clusters, internal-only tooling without user impact.
- Constraint: dedicated SRE headcount available = 1.5 FTEs for the campaign; product teams must contribute at least one engineering lead per service.

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Connor Hayes (eng-sre) — overall coordinator and timeline owner.
- Reliability liaisons: one assigned engineer from each product area (hosted-api, dedicated, private).
- Observability owner: Maya Patel (observability) — dashboard templates and metric wiring.
- Oncall integration: Samir Gupta (sre/ops) — pager and routing changes.
- Product QA: Elena Ortiz — acceptance and validation runs for SLOs.

Workstreams (parallel):
1) Inventory & risk scoring (weeks 1-3)
  - Create a short form to capture service, owner, user surface area, key metrics, current alerts.
  - Score services for user impact and incident cost to prioritize first 28.

2) Definition & baseline (weeks 2-5)
  - For prioritized services, run a 72-hour baseline data pull to propose SLO targets (e.g., availability 99.9% or latency P95 200ms).
  - Document SLO rationale and what user outcome it protects.

3) Implementation & small-batch rollout (weeks 4-9)
  - Provide SLO templates (prometheus/observability DSL, example alert rules).
  - Team pairing: SRE + product engineer pair to implement and test.
  - Create minimal remediation playbooks and add to runbooks repo.

4) Validation & oncall integration (weeks 6-10)
  - Run simulated degradations (traffic shaping, added latency) to validate alert fidelity and reduce false positives.
  - Wire alerts to oncall routes and create escalation flow.

5) Handoff & measurement (week 9-10)
  - Handoff checklist: owner confirmation, runbook reviewed, dashboard available, incident postmortem template included.
  - Measurement: capture initial error budget burn for 30 days and report.

Resource runway (10-week view):
- Week 1-3: Inventory sprint — SREs 0.6 FTE, Observability 0.4 FTE, Product liaisons 0.2 FTE (per team).
- Week 4-6: Definition sprint — SREs 0.8 FTE, Observability 0.5 FTE, QA 0.3 FTE.
- Week 7-9: Implementation sprint — SREs 1.0 FTE, Product engineers variable (0.4 FTE avg), Documentation 0.2 FTE.
- Week 10: Cutover & reporting — SREs 0.5 FTE, Oncall owner 0.5 FTE, Program lead overhead 0.2 FTE.

Cross-team mapping format (deliverable):
- CSV-style table with columns: service_name, product_area, primary_owner, secondary_owner, critical_metric, proposed_slo, risk_score, sprint_assignment, completion_status.
- This mapping will be stored in the runbooks repo and a live Confluence table.

Handoff checkpoints (gated):
- Gate 1 (Definition complete): Proposed SLO + baseline documented and accepted by product + SRE.
- Gate 2 (Implementation complete): Metric ingestion and dashboard present; alert fires in staging.
- Gate 3 (Oncall-ready): Playbook reviewed; alert routed; runbook links added to oncall rotation.

Risk register (top items):
- Low observability in a service: mitigation = add short-lived exporters and synthetic probes before deadline.
- Product bandwidth shortage: mitigation = narrow SLO to a minimal customer-impacting metric and defer extras.
- Alert noise causing ignored SLO alerts: mitigation = require a successful synthetic test and 1-week monitoring before routing to primary oncall.

Success metrics and reporting cadence:
- Weekly pulse: count of services in each stage of pipeline, current FTE burn rate, top 3 blockers.
- Biweekly stakeholder sync: program lead + product leads + observability owner.
- Post-campaign report (week 12): adoption rate, early error budget burns, incident delta and recommended follow-ups.

Communication plan:
- Slack channel: #slo-campaign (announcements, blockers).
- Weekly digest: short email + Confluence update every Friday.
- Office hours: twice-weekly SRE drop-in for implementation help.

Templates & artifacts attached (in repo):
- SLO template examples: availability, latency, and throughput examples.
- Playbook checklist: immediate steps, rollback criteria, and annotated runbook snippet.
- Inventory form link: short survey to capture owners and metrics.

Acceptance criteria for a service to be considered 'adopted':
- SLO documented in Confluence with owner + rationale.
- Dashboard with live metric and alert visible in staging and prod.
- Playbook with at least 3 remediation steps and a postmortem template.
- Oncall routing configured and tested once.

Next steps (first 7 days):
- Day 1: Kickoff meeting with all liaisons; share inventory form.
- Day 2-5: SREs begin automated discovery of metric endpoints and quick risk scoring.
- End of week 1: publish prioritized list of 28 services and assign sprint owners.

Appendix: Quick example SLO definition (for a text generation endpoint)
- Service: /v1/generate (hosted-api)
- Objective: Ensure useful responses within latency and correctness bounds for synchronous calls.
- Proposed SLO: 99.85% of requests complete with status=200 and P95 latency < 350ms over a 30-day window.
- Key metric sources: request_status_code, request_latency_ms, inference_queue_depth.
- Alerting: page when 10-minute error rate > 0.5% and sustained for 15m.

Notes and open questions:
- Which 28 services are considered 'critical' should be vendor-neutral and reflect production traffic weight — program lead to propose list by end of week 1.
- Need to confirm whether Dedicated customers require different SLO windows; product lead to clarify.
- Estimate for synthetic probe coverage and cost to be provided by observability team in week 2.

End of document.
